approach: Add a hold as an append-only per-job record (`athena.hold/1`, `<job>/hold-<n>.json`, state `held` or `released`; highest `n` wins). `JobRecords::on_hold()` is true when the latest hold record is `held` and the job is in a state drain works: Queued, Proposed (read by `go`, by drain's read-ahead, or made by approving a steward proposal) or Dispatched (an interrupted job drain retries). `RealSteps::entry_of` copies it into a new `PlanEntry.on_hold` flag; `plan_entry` and `queue` both go through `entry_of`, so a re-made entry keeps the flag. `Plan::build_with`, which every plan builder calls, refuses an `on_hold` entry first with reason "on hold" and an empty `missing`; dependents are held by the existing dependency loop. `Drain::prepare` does not read a held item, and `batches_for` drops everything in `plan.refused`, so drain never dispatches it at any priority. `athena plan` already prints a refusal with empty `missing` as a `held` line. `Athena::set_hold` and `release_hold` copy `set_priority`, but `set_hold` accepts any open job state and `release_hold` checks the latest hold record rather than the job state. Priority is untouched. The docs/records.md edit is dropped (it was outside the deliverables).

decisions.choice: Enforce the hold in `Plan::build_with` through a new `PlanEntry.on_hold: bool` (serde skipped when false); the reason text is built in plan.rs.
decisions.reason: The plan decides what drain dispatches: `Drain::prepare` builds it, `athena plan` prints it, and `batches_for` (drain.rs:3034) dispatches only its groups. Holding there means `Plan::build` alone never orders a held item, so the unit test covers all four priorities, and dependents are held by the existing loop (plan.rs:700-726) with no new logic. `PlanEntry::bare` plus `..bare` spreads keep most literals compiling.

rejected.option: A new `Steps::on_hold` method merged into `Drain::prepare`'s `held` map (drain.rs:2302).
rejected.why: The rule would live only in the CLI crate, so `Plan::build` would still order a held item; it also needs a stub override and a second dependents loop, and the paused-line reason says 'its line is paused'.
They would not appear in `athena plan`, which the request requires, and `athena status` would lose them.

rejected.option: Lower the priority or add a fifth 'held' priority level.
rejected.why: That is the failure the request describes; it would also change `Priority::parse`, the caps and the order, all out of scope.

decisions.choice: Hold state is a separate record type `HoldRecord { job, n, at, state: held|released }` at `<job>/hold-<n>.json`, numbered per job, highest `n` wins. No reason text.
decisions.reason: Records are append-only (PriorityRecord doc, records.rs:520-523), so release is a later record. A separate type leaves `athena.priority/1` and its validator alone, so hold stays independent of priority. The optional reason text is omitted as the smallest design.

rejected.why: It changes an existing `deny_unknown_fields` schema (records.rs:524), and latest-record-wins would tie hold to priority: setting a priority would release the hold.

rejected.option: A free-text hold reason shown in plan.
rejected.why: Not needed; adds validation and a longer line.

decisions.choice: Revised for finding 2: a hold is allowed on any job drain can work, not only Queued. `JobRecords::on_hold()` = latest hold record is `held` AND `state()` is Queued, Proposed or Dispatched. `Athena::set_hold` refuses a job in any other state (Declined, Blocked, Closed) with 'only an open request can be held', refuses a job running now (`Athena::running`, status.rs:1079), and refuses a job whose latest hold record is already `held`. `Athena::release_hold` checks only the latest hold record ('is not on hold' if there is none or it is `released`); it does not look at job state.
decisions.reason: Drain's queue is `approved_work` (Proposed, steward.rs:487-511) + `queued_work` (Queued or Proposed, steward.rs:405-444) + `interrupted_work` (Dispatched with no process, steward.rs:450-483), assembled in `RealSteps::queue` (drain.rs:4471-4525). `JobRecords::state()` (store.rs:119-140) turns Queued into Proposed as soon as a reading or invocation exists, which `athena plan`'s read-ahead (drain.rs:2243-2266) or `athena go` causes. Tying the hold to Queued would let drain dispatch an item the operator held just after `athena plan` read it, and would make steward-approved items unholdable. Using the latest hold record for release means a hold is never lost silently: it stays visible and releasable whatever the job state does next, and a hold on a job that closed or was declined is simply inert (on_hold() false because the state is not worked) and still releasable.

rejected.option: Queued only (the previous plan, mirroring `set_priority`, reading.rs:1008).
rejected.why: The critic's finding: the hold silently stops counting once the job is read, and drain then dispatches it.

rejected.option: Hold on any state including Closed.
rejected.why: A hold on a closed or declined job does nothing; refusing it tells the operator the job is not in the queue.
Blocked jobs are retried by `athena go` only; they are not in drain's queue (steward.rs:411), so a hold would mean nothing.

decisions.choice: In `Plan::build_with`, an `on_hold` entry wins over an incomplete plan: it is kept in `pending` and put first in the held list, never listed as 'lacking'. `Drain::prepare` skips an on-hold entry when deciding which items to read (drain.rs:2243-2248 gets an `on_hold` check before the `missing()` check).
decisions.reason: The operator sees 'on hold', the actionable reason, and a held item must not cost a reader call or budget.

rejected.option: Hold only entries whose plan is complete.
rejected.why: An unread held item would be read and paid for, and shown as 'lacking' instead of 'on hold'.

decisions.choice: Show the hold in `athena status` through a new `JobLine.on_hold: bool` (serde skipped when false) and a ' · on hold' suffix in `plan_suffix`; it is not the existing `JobLine.hold`, which means a disk-space hold.
decisions.reason: The operator needs to see held items in the open-work list. Reusing `hold: Option<String>` would print '(still queued)' text that means something else (display.rs:1068).

rejected.why: Held jobs would look like queued ones and the operator would not know why drain skips them.

decisions.choice: Do not edit docs/records.md (finding 1). The record type is documented in the doc comments of `HoldRecord`, in CHANGELOG.md and in the command help.
decisions.reason: It is not a listed deliverable; no test or crate reads docs/records.md for schema coverage (a search for `athena.priority/1` outside records/ finds only docs files, records.rs, store.rs and CHANGELOG.md).

risks.risk: Adding a field to `PlanEntry` or `JobLine` breaks a struct literal that lists every field.
risks.mitigation: Seen literals use `..PlanEntry::bare(..)`; the compiler finds any other (hestia.rs:7369, drain.rs:5037, 6305, 7260, display.rs:2623 and 2676). The last step is a full `cargo clippy --all-targets` pass.

risks.risk: A drain whose only items are all held might not end cleanly or might spin. I read `batches_for` (drain.rs:3034), which drops refused items, but did not trace the whole loop's end condition.
risks.mitigation: The real-steps test asserts the drain returns with no job run and no landing; paused items, which also sit in `plan.refused`, already end a drain (tests/drain.rs:995, 1332).

risks.risk: A held, running job: `set_hold` refuses a job running now, but a job that starts running after the hold is set (for example `athena go` on a held job) is not stopped by it.
risks.mitigation: `go` is an explicit operator act, not drain. After it, `on_hold()` stays true while the state is Dispatched and the job is run by nobody else; the latest record stays `held` and is releasable, so nothing is lost silently. The store test covers Dispatched.

risks.risk: A hold on a job that later closes or is declined stays in the records as `held`, and status drops the mark.
risks.mitigation: Intended: such a job is not in drain's queue, so the hold has no effect, and `release` still works on the latest record. The store test checks `on_hold()` false for Closed and Declined.

risks.risk: `Drain::prepare` for an interrupted held job: its entry is refused, so drain does not retry it.
risks.mitigation: That is the requested behavior; the read-loop skip applies only to items not already `read` or `interrupted` (drain.rs:2232), and `batches_for` drops the refusal. The store test covers the Dispatched state.

After `release_hold`, the same drain asks the lander for that job. A second real-steps test (finding 2) queues a job, runs `athena.go(..)` so it is Proposed, confirms `queued_ids` lists it, holds it, drains with no dispatch, releases, and drains with a dispatch.

demonstrations.method: records.rs unit test `a_hold_record_has_a_path_a_schema_and_round_trips`: schema 'athena.hold/1', path `.../hold-1.json`, parse and re-serialize equal, `check_record_file` accepts the canonical path and returns `Misplaced` for another number, n=0 is `Invalid`, an unknown state fails to parse. store.rs test via `Records::from_parts` with hold-2 listed before hold-1: `holds` ordered by `n`, and `on_hold()` follows the highest `n` for a Queued, a Proposed and a Dispatched job and is false for a Closed or Declined job.
demonstrations.command: cargo test -p athena-data a_hold_record && cargo test -p athena-core holds_load_in_order_of_n
demonstrations.observes: Round-trip equality, `Misplaced` at the wrong path, `Invalid` for n=0, `holds` sorted by `n`, `on_hold()` true/false as listed.
demonstrations.fails_without: Without the `AnyRecord` variant `check_record_file` returns a Parse error; without the per-job vector and sort, `holds` follows file order and the sorted assert fails; with a Queued-only `on_hold()` the Proposed and Dispatched asserts fail.
demonstrations.seam: `AnyRecord::parse`, `check_record_file`, `Records::from_parts` (store.rs:355-460), all exist. Steps 2 and 3 add `HoldRecord` and `JobRecords.holds`.

demonstrations.method: The help test runs `athena --help`, `athena hold --help`, `athena release --help` through the binary (as the existing help test at tests/drain.rs:2522-2541). The dispatch from main.rs through commands.rs to `Athena::set_hold`/`release_hold` is evidenced by the criterion 4 binary test, which commits through it. As a diff check, `git diff -- crates/athena-cli/src/main.rs crates/athena-cli/src/commands.rs crates/athena-core/src/reading.rs` must show the two `Command` variants with `///` doc comments, the two dispatch arms, and the two new `Athena` methods modeled on `set_priority`.
demonstrations.command: cargo test -p athena-cli --test drain hold_and_release_help_say_what_they_do && cargo test -p athena-cli --test drain hold_and_release_commands_append_records_and_refuse_what_they_must
demonstrations.observes: Help text holds 'open', 'drain' and 'priority' for hold, and 'release' lifts it; `hold-1.json` and `hold-2.json` appear after the binary calls.
demonstrations.fails_without: Without the subcommands `hold --help` exits non-zero and the help test fails; without the dispatch to the new methods no hold record is committed and the criterion 4 test fails.
demonstrations.seam: The binary via `CARGO_BIN_EXE_athena`; no new double.

demonstrations.method: Reviewer diff check: a new bullet under `## [Unreleased]` / `### Added` must name the `athena.hold/1` record, `athena hold` and `athena release`, that drain skips a held item at any priority (queued, read or interrupted), the `held` line in `athena plan` and the status mark. Failing that, the diff has no such bullet.
demonstrations.observes: The bullet is present and written for an outside reader.

demonstrations.method: Diff check: the stat must list none of athena.toml, defaults.toml, .github/workflows, nor the test bodies for rejected or failed dependencies (reading.rs:3102-3202, plan.rs:1288) and `job_history` itself; the filtered test run must pass. Failing that, any of those paths appears in the stat.
demonstrations.command: git diff --stat && cargo test -p athena-core rejected
demonstrations.observes: No governance file or `job_history` change in the stat; the rejected-dependency tests pass.

demonstrations.method: Run the three recorded checks on the final tree. Existing tests change only by adding `on_hold: false` where a struct literal lists every field.
demonstrations.command: cargo fmt --all --check && cargo clippy --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings && cargo test --locked
demonstrations.fails_without: A `PlanEntry` or `JobLine` literal left without the new field fails to compile; an unrelated behavior change fails an existing test.
demonstrations.seam: The repository's own checks; no new seam.
